newsitem.title: USA: Peapod Inc shares steady after offering.
newsitem.headline: Peapod Inc shares steady after offering.

text.p: Shares of Peapod Inc traded at 16-1/2 in the late morning Wednesday after its initial offering at $16 a share, which raised $64 million for the online shopping and delivery service.

Earlier, the stock traded as high as 18-1/2, as institutional investors bought shares in the aftermarket, according to Kathleen Smith, portfolio manager for Renaissance Capital Corp of Greenwich, Conn.
"They had a good order book for the deal and many of the institutional investors who bought shares on the offering also were committed to buying shares in the aftermarket," she said.
Shares of Peapod were priced at $16 each late on Tuesday, the top of its estimated range of $15 to $16, according to lead underwriter Smith Barney.

The size and price range of the offering were increased on the eve of the IPO pricing when Peapod agreed to sell four million shares at $15 to $16 each, up from an original plan to sell 3.6 million shares at $13 to $15.
By late Wednesday morning, more than three million shares had traded.
Ryan Jacob, director of research for the IPO Value Monitor, said Peapod shares traded around 16-1/2 after a strong opening, reflecting some early profit taking.
"It opened up strongly. We're seeing the pullback as investors realize a short-term gain," he added.
Analysts said Peapod is still in the developmental stage and is not yet generating a profit, which has raised questions in the minds of some investors.
"There are the skeptics out there," Smith said. "But they (Peapod and others) are early players in what is going to be a very big market."
